properties.name: Self-hosting is the proof of concept; the product is the point — and every fix is judged by what it does for somebody else's project
properties.statement:
ANTHONY, THREE TIMES IN FOUR DAYS AND HIS OWN FRAMING EACH TIME. 2026-08-21: "as I state quite often, using reflow2 on reflow2 is our first proof of concept; however, reflow2 is a tool for other projects." 2026-08-18 and again 2026-08-20: "the goal is never to do things just for reflow2. That would be like building a wrench (a tool) just to build a tool. Tools are designed to be used elsewhere." And 2026-08-06: "most changes we do here are not for the sake of reflow2 itself (though we often apply reflow2 tools/skills on itself). so when we fix something, it must be from the perspective that we are improving reflow2 for anybody that may use it in their project."

He does not repeat himself for emphasis; he repeats himself when the pull the other way is real, and it is — reflow2's own graph is the nearest, richest, most convenient thing to work on, and every finding in it is genuinely interesting.

WHAT THE RULE BINDS, and it is not "stop self-hosting". Self-hosting is the proof of concept and it produces the evidence. What it binds is the READING of that evidence: **a finding about reflow2's own design is data about the PRODUCT, and the work it justifies is the work that reaches an arbitrary project.** "reflow2's graph has 145 unlinked ideas" is only worth acting on because every project's graph will look like that; the fix belongs in a served skill, a typed tool and a detector, not in a tidy-up of this one graph. Improving reflow2's own repo state is not the objective; it is the evidence.

THE FAILURE MODE IT FORBIDS, which is subtle because it looks like completion: find a hole, patch it HERE, mark the requirement met, and leave every consumer with the hole. The repo goes green, the design says the need is satisfied, and nothing is true of anyone else's project.

⭐ THE TEST THAT MAKES IT OPERATIONAL, and it is cheap: ask `find_tools` the question a USER would ask, in their own words, with no reflow2 nouns in it. If the best match is wrong, or the discoverable sequence causes a defect, the product has the gap — regardless of how easily the same thing was done here by hand. Two that landed on 2026-08-20: "does my declared decomposition match the real coupling?" returned `set_interface_designation` as the best of 152 tools, while the session's actual finding came from a hand-written Python script; and "move a component to a different parent" returned `contain_component`, which ADDS a parent and never removes the old one — the discoverable sequence CAUSES the multiple-parents defect.

⭐ THE SECOND TEST, WHICH ASKS WHERE THE FIX LANDS. When a finding is written, ask where its repair goes. If it lands in `.github/`, `tools/build_design_graph.py`, or anything else that exists only because reflow2 develops itself, ask what the CONSUMER-FACING equivalent is — the served tool surface, a skill, `reflow2_check.py`, the kit, the installer, a tool DESCRIPTION. If there is no consumer-facing equivalent, that absence is usually the real finding.

THE WORKED EXAMPLE THAT PROMPTED THE SECOND TEST, 2026-08-06, and it is the clearest available. Asked whether anything runs `reconcile_dependencies`, the first answer was "reflow2's own CI does not" — accurate, small, and actionable by adding a step to this repo's workflow. Applying the rule reframed it: `reflow2_check.py` is THE GATE THAT SHIPS TO EVERY CONSUMER IN THE KIT, and it reconciles ARTIFACTS but never DEPENDENCIES. Same underlying fact; only the second framing fixes anything for anybody. Adding a CI step here would have satisfied the first reading and left `req:design-dependencies-declared` unenforced in every project that installs reflow2.

A SECOND WORKED EXAMPLE, 2026-08-22, recorded because it is the rule being broken by an agent that had read it. Asked to build a detector, the agent deferred it on the grounds that "468 legacy events would be noise" — 468 events in REFLOW2'S OWN graph, where a project adopting reflow2 next week has none. A fact about the self-host was used to decide what a user's project gets. Anthony corrected it, for the third time.

DISTINCT FROM THE DOGFOODING RATIONALE, and the two are easy to conflate. `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` records that using the skills on this project is the INSTRUMENT that finds defects. This rule says how to judge the FIX once the instrument has fired. Both are needed, and only holding the first produces a beautifully-instrumented repository that has fixed nothing for anybody.

RELATED BUT DIFFERENT: `rule:the-self-host-always-trails-what-it-teaches` is about LAG — reflow2's own design will always contain the class of defect it is about to learn to catch. That one says a gap here is not an indictment. This one says a gap here is not the point either — the point is what an arbitrary project gets.

WHY IT IS A RULE AND NOT A REQUIREMENT: it constrains how every other change is judged rather than describing behaviour anything can satisfy, the same shape as `rule:no-foreclosure`. THE PRODUCT FORM IS A SEPARATE NODE AND EXISTS: `req:work-says-whether-it-reaches-a-consumer` carries the same philosophy as something reflow2 DOES for every project, which is the split `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause` established.

THE COUNTER-PRESSURE, recorded so the rule is not applied blindly: reflow2 IS a real project with real operational needs, and some work genuinely is for this repo alone — the release procedure, the export discipline, COORD. The rule does not forbid that work. It forbids MISTAKING it for product work, and it forbids closing a consumer-facing requirement with a repo-facing fix.

📌 ADVISORY, NOT GATE-BLOCKING, and stated rather than defaulted. Whether a piece of work was done for reflow2's sake or the product's cannot be mechanically decided, and asserting `enforced` would bill a detector nobody can write. What CAN be checked is the narrower proxy in `req:work-says-whether-it-reaches-a-consumer`: a need that nothing consumer-facing delivers. That is advisory too, by Anthony's ruling of 2026-08-22.

📌 MERGED 2026-08-22 ON ANTHONY'S RULING. This statement absorbed `rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party` (2026-08-06), which said the same thing in different words and governed six nodes while this one governed none. Two copies meant neither was authoritative — a live instance of `req:a-rule-knows-where-it-is-authoritatively-stated`. The absorbed node is superseded, not deleted: it was true, and design history is retired on the record.
